content:
- Model tends to overestimate prices in early days of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimates during sharp downward trends, particularly when true values dip below 70.
- Overreacts to recent high values (e.g., 75+), producing exaggerated peaks in forecast that don’t materialize.
- Shows persistent bias toward higher values in the first 5–10 days of forecast, then gradually converges toward true mean.
- Fails to capture mean reversion in the 10–20 day window; often holds high forecasts longer than actual price behavior.
- Overshoots after spikes, especially in the 70–75 range, then corrects sharply — model lags in recognizing the correction.
- Underestimates when true values are near or below 70, particularly in the 68–72 range.
- Forecast tends to be too optimistic in the final 5–10 days, especially when true values are trending downward.
